title: Dynamic speed adjustment via vertical finger drag during hold-to-read
description: While holding to read (RSVP playback), moving the finger up increases reading speed and moving it down decreases it, without releasing the hold gesture. Should feel continuous/analog rather than stepped, and respect the existing WPM range (100-1000).

title: Sync-to-audio: synchronized audio + RSVP playback
description: Major new feature: import an MP3 plus a time-coded text file, then sync the audio playback with the rapid-serial-visual word display so each word is shown in time with the spoken audio. Blocked on a research spike to settle on a supported time-coded text format (SRT, VTT, forced-alignment JSON, etc.) before implementation design.

title: Research time-coded text formats for audio sync
description: Evaluate candidate time-coded text formats for the sync-to-audio feature: SRT, WebVTT, forced-alignment JSON (e.g. Whisper/aeneas/gentle output), custom per-word timestamp format, etc. Decide which format(s) to accept as import, how word-level (not just line-level) timing will be derived if the format is only line/sentence-level, and how users will produce/obtain a time-coded transcript for their own MP3s. Output: a short decision doc/ADR feeding the sync-to-audio implementation design.

title: Smart pause skip for synced audio (like Overcast Smart Speed)
description: For the sync-to-audio feature, automatically detect and shorten/skip silent gaps between spoken words or sentences in the synced audio, analogous to Overcast's Smart Speed (which trims silence from podcasts without altering pitch). Goal: keep the RSVP word display moving at a natural pace even through pauses in speech, rather than stalling the reader on dead air. Depends on having per-word/segment timing data from the sync-to-audio work, so silence gaps can be identified and compressed or auto-advanced through.
